Weighted Voting and Power Indices

CountingPermutationsLogic
Game: Players with different numbers of votes team up to reach a target. Find out who really has the power.
How to play: Change the target and the votes in the brackets, tick “Compute indices”, and compare each player's share of power with their share of votes.

PlayerVotesBanzhafShapley-Shubik

Look for the math

In a weighted voting system [q: w₁, …, wₙ] player i controls wᵢ votes and a decision passes when the votes for it reach the quota q. Having votes is not the same as having power. In [5: 3, 2, 1] the first two players decide everything together and the one-vote player never matters: a dummy.

Banzhaf: who can break a coalition

A coalition is any non-empty group of players; it is winning if its votes reach q. A player is critical to a winning coalition if the coalition loses without them. The Banzhaf index of a player is the number of times they are critical over the total number of times anyone is. In the starting system [6: 4, 3, 2, 1] the counts are 5, 3, 3, 1 out of 12: the 3-vote and 2-vote players have exactly the same power.

Shapley-Shubik: who tips the balance

Now let the players join one at a time, in one of the n! possible orders. The pivotal player is the one whose arrival first brings the total up to q. If q is at most the total of all the votes, every order has exactly one pivotal player. The Shapley-Shubik index is the share of orders in which a player is pivotal: 10, 6, 6, 2 of 24 for [6: 4, 3, 2, 1]. The two indices often differ, but they always agree on who is a dummy.

How it is counted

The applet listed all 2ⁿ coalitions and all n! orders, and for 13 or more players n! was too big for it. Here the orders are counted by coalition: player i is pivotal in |S|!·(n − 1 − |S|)! orders for every group S that loses without i and wins with them. The test compared both indices with the applet's own enumeration on over 6,000 systems of up to 7 players. When the quota is more than all the votes together, the applet still named player 1 pivotal in every order; with no winning coalition at all, this page says so instead.

Start from [6: 4, 3, 2, 1] and raise the quota one step at a time up to 10. When does the 1-vote player lose all power, and when does it get it back?
